title: Cap. VIII Arg. 10: God as spiritual sun — reprobation from foresight of putting an obstacle to grace
pass_a_gloss: God is as it were a certain Sun everywhere diffusing the rays of spiritual grace: Therefore as much as in him is, he imparts spiritual grace unto all, unless they put an obstacle to the diffused rays of his grace. That therefore he leaves certain ones void of grace and reprobates them, happens thence, that he foresaw these as putting an obstacle to his grace. Reprobation therefore is from this foresighted evil use of free will.
pass_b_english: Tenth: God is as it were a Sun everywhere diffusing rays of spiritual grace. Therefore, as much as in him lies, he imparts spiritual grace to all, unless they put an obstacle to those diffused rays. That he leaves some void of grace and reprobates them happens because he foresaw them putting an obstacle to his grace. So reprobation is from that foresighted evil use of free will.
source_text: Deus est quasi Sol quidam radios gratiae spiritualis ubique diffundens: Ergo quantum in se est, gratiam spiritualem omnibus impertit, nisi diffusis gratiae suae radiis obicem ponant. Quod igitur quosdam gratiae expertes relinquit et reprobat, id inde evenit, quod praevidit hosce ut obicem ponentes gratiae suae. Reprobatio igitur est ex praeviso hoc malo usu liberi arbitrii.
